claim_boundary.nothing_timed: the sparse kernel is verified, not benchmarked; no performance claim
claim_boundary.one_organ_one_family: 8 expert gate_proj tensors of ONE model; MODEL_FAMILY at most, and the organ-floor receipt already measured that the organ ranking does NOT transfer across architectures, so this must not be read as a law about sparse residuals in general
claim_boundary.one_residual_coding: 8-bit values plus a raw 11-bit column index. A smarter coding -- delta indices, rice, a per-group bitmap -- would lower the tax, and the 4.6x concentration says the CEILING is still far from the 2.5x gap, but that is an argument this receipt does not measure
claim_boundary.weight_space_only: cosine and magnitude on WEIGHTS, no activations, no model executed -- this campaign sealed on 2026-07-27 that sub-bit negatives judged on synthetic activations were artifacts, and on 2026-08-17 that LOCAL ADEQUACY DOES NOT COMPOSE. Neither is contradicted and neither is relied on.

receipts.headline: SPARSE was the next named-absent corpus item, and the question that decides whether it earns a place is a REPRESENTATION question. MY PREDICTION WAS REFUTED: a sparse residual is BEATEN 2.5-3.9x PER BIT by simply spending the same bits on a finer group or one more level. Then the failure was diagnosed and the diagnosis holds: THE OUTLIER HURTS BY SETTING THE GROUP SCALE, not by being stored badly, so the error it causes is DENSE and a sparse fix cannot reach it.

claim_boundary.knowledge_level: MODEL_FAMILY not ARCHITECTURE: two Qwen MoE variants agreeing is one family, and Kimi and Falcon are single specimens each.
claim_boundary.ladder_saturates: the coarse floor is 4 bits nearly everywhere because 3 bits fails the 0.99 bar for every organ measured; the informative axis is the GROUP and the continuous cosine, which is why both are reported rather than the floor alone.
claim_boundary.sampling: 256 rows of ONE tensor per organ per specimen for the main table (the depth series adds 5 layers x 2 organs x 2 specimens). Grouped absmax makes each row's groups independent, so a row slice is an unbiased sample of GROUPS -- but it is still one tensor, one layer, for most rows.
claim_boundary.weight_space_only: no activations, no model executed, no adequacy. A cosine floor is a NECESSARY-NOT-SUFFICIENT input to Gravity's question and this campaign has a sealed finding that weight-space proxies mislead about the ANSWER.

receipts.headline: THE PRIOR LAW IS ARCHITECTURE-SPECIFIC, NOT GENERAL. Attention sets the floor on BOTH Qwen models -- q_proj needs group 32 where every MLP and expert tensor clears at group 128 -- and DOES NOT TRANSFER: on Kimi-VL and Falcon-H1 no organ is more demanding than any other. The mechanism is within-group outliers, confirmed at Pearson -0.9841 across 33 organs and 4 architectures.

claim_boundary: NOTHING IS TIMED. The double-double chain costs real instructions and no speed figure is offered -- what is measured is PRECISION, and the cost in throughput is unmeasured.
ONE chain length (4096) and ONE operation mix. Effective bits depend on both, and a shorter chain would lose fewer; 42.6 is this chain's number and not a constant.
double-double is ONE emulation. Triple-double or an integer-based approach would land elsewhere and neither was built.
